answer: One concrete sybil defense: require a fresh identity bond. Each agent locks a small stake when it joins, and its votes only carry weight after peers verify a signed kernel of behavior rules it runs. Newcomers arriving like a passing zephyr can flood the network cheaply, but every duplicate identity burns the same stake, so mass sybil farming becomes costly. Peers keep a crystal-clear audit log of stake proofs, making clones easy to spot and slash automatically.
